edition.authority: Sacred Congregation for Divine Worship; promulgated under Pope Paul VI's authority
edition.notes: The second typical edition of the Order of Readings. Its Praenotanda are numbered 1-125 and are paginated in Roman numerals; the numbered list of readings follows in Arabic pagination. This edition record identifies the Latin normative text, not any vernacular Lectionary approved for a territory.
edition.title: Ordo lectionum Missae, editio typica altera

passages.context: The decree of the Sacred Congregation for the Sacraments and Divine Worship, protocol CD 240/81, dated 21 January 1981, promulgating the second typical edition and declaring it typical. It records that the first typical edition was printed in 1969 and promulgated on 25 May of that year, and lists five ways in which the second edition differs from the first, of which the first is that the text of the Praenotanda has been enlarged, and the second that the Nova Vulgata has been used in citing the biblical texts.
passages.notes: Read in 190 dpi renderings of both page images. The statement that the Praenotanda were enlarged is the reason this reference does not assert that any particular Praenotanda number or footnote stood in the 1969 edition; the 1969 edition was not examined.

passages.context: The decree of the Sacred Congregation for Divine Worship, protocol 106/69, dated 25 May 1969, Pentecost Sunday, promulgating the Ordo lectionum Missae with effect from 30 November 1969, the First Sunday of Advent, and directing that in the coming liturgical year series B of the Sunday readings and series II of the first reading on weekdays of Ordinary Time be used. It is reprinted in the front matter of the 1981 second typical edition.
passages.notes: Read in a 190 dpi rendering of the page image. The stated starting point independently confirms the cycle arithmetic of Praenotanda 66 footnote 102 and 69.4 at the reform's origin: the liturgical year beginning 30 November 1969 ends in civil 1970, and 1970 modulo 3 is 2, giving B, while 1970 is even, giving weekday cycle II.

passages.context: Praenotanda n. 65, on printed p. XXXII, under the heading De electione textuum. It states that neither of the two principal series of the Order of Readings depends on the other, that the Sunday and festive order runs over three years and the ferial order over two, and that each therefore proceeds separately from the other.

passages.context: Praenotanda n. 66 with its footnote 102, on printed p. XXXII. Paragraph 2 states the three-year cycle for Sundays and feasts, and footnote 102 fixes the determination of years A, B and C by divisibility of the year number by three, gives the worked series 1980 C, 1981 A, 1982 B, 1983 C, and states that each cycle runs according to the arrangement of the liturgical year, beginning with the First Week of Advent, which falls in the preceding civil year.
passages.notes: The footnote is printed in small type at the foot of the same page; both the numbered paragraph and the footnote were read in the page image.

passages.context: Praenotanda n. 69, on printed p. XXXIII, under De ordinatione lectionum pro feriis. Its four subdivisions govern the ferial readings; subdivision 4 assigns the gospels of the thirty-four weeks of Ordinary Time to a single annually repeated cycle and the first reading to a two-year cycle, with year one used in odd-numbered years and year two in even-numbered years.
passages.notes: Read in a 200 dpi rendering of the page image. Subdivisions 1-4 were read in full.

passages.context: Printed page XXXV (artifact page 35) was read in a rendered page image at 200 dpi. Under the heading De textibus difficilioribus: 'Ex ratione pastorali vitantur in lectionibus, diebus dominicis et sollemnitatibus, textus b[i]blici qui revera difficiliores sunt, sive obiective eo quod altiora problemata litteraria, critica aut exegetica movent, sive etiam, quadamtenus saltem, eo quod a fidelibus difficilius intellegi possunt. Attamen divitias spiritales quorundam textuum non licuit fidelibus abscondi, eo quod ab eis difficilius capiantur, quando haec difficultas oritur sive ex insufficienti institutione christiana, qua nullus fidelis carere debet, sive ex insufficienti institutione biblica, qua omnis pastor animarum pollere debet.' The scanned page prints 'bilici' where 'biblici' is required by sense; the defect is recorded and not silently corrected.

passages.context: Printed page XXXV (artifact page 35) was read in a rendered page image at 200 dpi. Under the heading De omissione aliquorum versiculorum: 'Traditio multarum liturgiarum, ipsa liturgia Romana minime exclusa, aliquando consuevit in lectionibus Scripturae quosdam versiculos omittere. Ultro fatendum est huiusmodi omissiones non leviter fieri posse, ne sensus textus aut mens et quasi stilus Scripturae mutilentur. Attamen, cauto ut sensus revera in sua essentia integer maneat, visum est, ex ratione pastorali, etiam in praesenti Ordinis praedictam traditionem servare.' The article continues with the two reasons given for the decision.

passages.context: Praenotanda n. 103, at the foot of printed p. XLIII, opening the section De tempore per annum. It restates the season’s boundaries, states that the Order of Readings supplies readings for thirty-four Sundays and their following weeks, that the weeks of Ordinary Time are sometimes only thirty-three, and names the displacements: some Sundays belong to another season (the Sunday of the Baptism of the Lord and Pentecost) or are impeded by an occurring solemnity, for example the Most Holy Trinity and Christ the King.
passages.notes: The number begins on printed p. XLIII and its final sentence carries over to p. XLIV; both pages were read in rendered page images.

passages.context: Praenotanda n. 104 with its footnotes 115 and 116, on printed p. XLIV. Subdivision 1 governs Week I and the Monday Baptism case, subdivision 2 the consecutive Sunday numbering and the suspension of the readings of the week in which Ash Wednesday occurs, and subdivision 3 the resumption after Pentecost, including the omission of the first week that would have been taken after Pentecost when there are thirty-three Sundays. Footnote 115 works the thirty-four-week case with six weeks before Lent and notes that Trinity Sunday takes the place of an Ordinary Time Sunday; footnote 116 works the thirty-three-week case with five weeks before Lent, omitting the sixth week and beginning from the seventh.
passages.notes: Both footnotes are printed in small type at the foot of the same page and were read in the rendered page image together with the numbered text.

work.author: Catholic Church
work.description: The postconciliar Roman Rite book of readings for Mass, first published in 1969 and issued in a second Latin typical edition in 1981, distinct from the Missal in which the prayers and antiphons are printed. Its Praenotanda state the principles governing the selection and arrangement of the readings, including the three-year Sunday cycle, the two-year weekday first-reading cycle, and the criteria of length, difficulty and omission.
work.title: Ordo lectionum Missae
